items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: Now this is how the Joe Thomas's come along, the Cab Callows, the Count Basies -- all of them made the after parties.

ctx.x: Now this is how the Joe Thomas's come along, the Cab Callows, the Count Basies -- all of them made the after parties. And Joe and I got to be real tight. Chu Berry was with Cab Calloway then, and they all would come up and they'd jam with us and what have you -- and he sat beside me and he went up and made one of those off the horn notes, and I would say, "How do you make that?" -- and he would say, "I just do it." Didn't encourage me ... I'm a youngster. But he didn't tell you nothing.

But Joe Thomas would tell you everything he knew. So I had a double situation there with Joe -- loved his playing, his showmanship, plus he would talk to you and tell you things. So to me, he was like a father. And we ended up being very good friends, and when I got to New York -- well, I was with Lionel Hampton and he was with Luntz Ford, and they got married here in Philadelphia, and I was supposed to be his best man, because I was working at Fay's Theatre and had a break and couldn't get there and I sent my…
